sub_scenario.one_line: public safety dispatcher: offer the 13:00 remote lead after preparing the agency board

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the agency dependency board and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The dispatch schedule review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I coordinate planned daytime exercises accurately from the agency dependency board.
What does the board clarify?
Which evacuation, medical, and traffic actions must happen before a public alert.
Someone new shadowed me in the coordination room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the overnight alerts into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
During the river evacuation, I placed road closure, shelter transport, and hospital diversion on the board before issuing the public message.
Did the sequence hold?
Yes. Every agency received the same workable order.
I can take a short evening radio check after a regular shift.
Does that make a midnight multi-agency call routine?
No. The call requires choosing the order for several agencies at once.
I archived last cycle's notes on the dispatch schedule and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
After four nights of storm alerts, I need a protected sleep block before I take command decisions.
Is that necessary even on a quiet night?
Yes. The accumulated recovery debt is the risk, not only the next alert.
A vendor call about the agency dependency board ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the coordination room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the overnight alerts.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the dispatch schedule records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
In a map-free wildfire call, I announced the evacuation route before confirming ambulance access, forcing a last-minute reroute.
Why did that happen?
I was tired and relied on radio fragments instead of a shared board.
I sketched next week's plan for the overnight alerts before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the agency dependency board updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My asthma worsens with overnight smoke exposure, so remote daytime coordination is the health-safe alternative.
Could you still support the team?
Yes, by preparing the board and joining after sleep from a clean-air location.
The commissioner says taking the 00:00 chair will make me the face of the response.
Does that address the operational conditions?
No. It ignores the smoke exposure and the missing board.
I closed the week by updating the coordination room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The commissioner wants me to chair a midnight wildfire coordination room. What terms should I set?
